solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mix with general public as royal personage? Get lost!

definitions.text: Mix with general public as royal personage?
definitions.meaning: royals stroll informally among crowds, meeting people on an unscheduled public stroll
informally, to disappear or go missing, as an item that cannot be found

explanation.surface: A royal mingling with the crowd, then a curt instruction to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: The royal sense is the public stroll begun by the Queen in 1970; the second is the slang sense of something vanishing. 'Get lost!' reads as rudeness, but it is a plain definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a royal's informal stroll through crowds and, colloquially, an object going missing.

clue.text: Something sticky kisser served up

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: kisser is slang for the face, as is mug

explanation.surface: A sticky item that someone's face has been served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reverses MUG in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Adhesive or chewing confection is a typical sticky substance.

clue.text: Bridge player has rubbished this game

parts.note: the four bridge players are named by compass points, so West is W

indicators.note: rubbished suggests the letters of this are trashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A bridge player sneers at some lesser card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge player' sounds like a person at the table, but bridge writers label the seats North, South, East and West, so it is a single letter; 'rubbished' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Whist is the trick-taking card game from which bridge developed.

clue.text: Hit on victim, sucker

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or strike
prey is a victim of a hunter

explanation.surface: Someone strikes an easy target, a gullible sucker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sucker' looks like a dupe, but it means a fish with a sucking mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: This eel-like fish attaches to hosts with a suckered mouth, so it is literally a sucker.

clue.text: A European bar somewhere in Italy where trip abroad might begin

parts.note: a rod is a bar of metal or wood
Rome is the Italian capital

explanation.surface: A bar on the Continent, say in Italy, where a journey overseas may start.
explanation.definitionFit: An airfield is a place from which flights, and so foreign journeys, depart.

clue.text: Open entrance in orange and green

indicators.note: the entrance of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of orange is used

parts.note: vert is green in heraldry

explanation.surface: An open doorway in orange and green paintwork.
explanation.walkthrough: VERT is the heraldic word for green.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open is done in plain view, not hidden.

clue.text: High-speed traveller in theory on yacht at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or disordered, so the letters of on yacht are jumbled

explanation.surface: A speedy theoretical traveller aboard a boat out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges ON YACHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Physicists posit this hypothetical particle as always moving faster than light.

clue.text: Assimilating conclusion of case, father backs judge

indicators.note: assimilating means taking in, so one piece absorbs the other
backs means the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter, here from case

explanation.surface: A father supporting a judge's verdict at the end of a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' turns FR into RF; 'Assimilating' puts E, from 'conclusion of case', inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee is the official who adjudicates a game, so the short form means one who judges.

clue.text: Great stocking is ending on thigh — lovely!

indicators.note: stocking means holding in stock, so the outer word contains the rest

parts.note: raving, as in a raving beauty, means great or remarkable

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter, here from thigh

explanation.surface: An admirer of hosiery praises a stocking ending at the thigh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking' looks like hosiery but signals containment of IS plus H.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravishing describes beauty so great it enraptures, close to gorgeous.

clue.text: Figure touring near capitals of troubled lands at regular intervals

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the number surrounds the rest

parts.note: forty is a number, a figure
nigh is an old word for near

indicators.note: capitals are the initial letters of troubled and lands

explanation.surface: A person travelling around nearby war-torn countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' signals the number going round the rest; 'capitals of' takes the first letters of the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Happening every two weeks is a fixed recurring interval.

clue.text: West perhaps welcoming reversal of brief glitch in automated communications device

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the name holds the rest

parts.note: Mae West was a Hollywood actress, so West suggests her first name

indicators.note: reversal of means the shortened word runs backwards
brief means cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a gremlin is a mysterious fault or glitch in machinery

explanation.surface: Someone in the West welcomes the reversal of a minor bug in an automated messaging system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' drops the last letter of the glitch word, 'reversal of' turns it round, and 'welcoming' puts it inside the actress's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: This word-processing feature combines a template with an address list to send personalised letters automatically.

clue.text: Head of course again in position on cricket field

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, from course

parts.note: over, as in do it over, means again

explanation.surface: A course leader repeats a lesson on cricket fielding positions.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, cover is a fielding position on the off side, square of the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Cover point, shortened, is a named place where a fielder stands.

clue.text: Rent-collecting ministry was fast and effective

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so the ministry holds the other piece

parts.note: MoD is the UK Ministry of Defence
rent is the past tense of rend, as is tore

explanation.surface: A government department collecting rent proved quick and efficient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid to a landlord; it is the past tense of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: To motor informally means to make rapid, effective progress.

clue.text: Ship takes me back across current

indicators.note: across means spanning, so the two letters of me straddle the other piece

parts.note: in means current or fashionable
in football a sweeper is a defender, one of the backs

explanation.surface: A boat carries someone home over a strong current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' tempts as a reversal signal, but it is a football defender's position; 'across' has me spanning the word for current.
explanation.definitionFit: This naval vessel clears explosive devices from shipping lanes.

clue.text: Something added in assayin' enzyme

indicators.note: in places the addition within the dropped-g word

parts.note: assaying means trying, so with the g dropped it is tryin'
PS, a postscript, is something added to a letter

explanation.surface: An addition slipped in during an assay test of a lab enzyme.
explanation.definitionFit: This digestive protein from the pancreas breaks down proteins in the gut.

clue.text: Dashing like a fly, arguably, did you say?

indicators.note: did you say signals a word heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: a gnat is a small fly, so a coined adjective for it is gnatty

explanation.surface: Someone asks if being dashing resembles a fly.
explanation.walkthrough: The silent G drops out when the coined word is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashing and smart both describe someone stylishly dressed.

clue.text: Excellent access to penthouse suite?

definitions.meaning: first-rate, of the highest class or rank
the highest set of stairs leads up to a penthouse

explanation.surface: Superb way up to the luxury suite on the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the uppermost staircase; figuratively the best rank, as in premier sporting leagues.

clue.text: Inaccurate summing-up, being disagreeable

parts.note: off means wrong, as in off target
a summing-up comes at the close, an ending

explanation.surface: A judge's wrong summing-up proves annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: Offending things cause displeasure or offence, so are unpleasant.

clue.text: Low-down supporter, puppet of an old Labour leader?

parts.note: Michael Foot led the UK Labour Party 1980-83; of gives the possessive S
a tool or puppet is someone used by another

explanation.surface: A low-down stooge, the puppet of a former Labour chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low-down supporter' reads as a disreputable ally; it is a seat that props feet near the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: This low stool supports the feet, so it is a supporter close to the floor.

clue.text: Here's our staggering, overwhelming power, as Spider-Man or Batman?

indicators.note: overwhelming means covering over, so the jumble surrounds the other piece
staggering means reeling unsteadily, so the letters of here's our are jumbled

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A boast of astonishing strength, worthy of a comic-book hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staggering' rearranges HERESOUR; 'overwhelming' wraps it round P.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are comic-book crime fighters with extraordinary abilities, examples of the costumed hero.

clue.text: Again, call on minister is exactly what's needed

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a minister's title
it means the very thing, as in that's it

explanation.surface: A minister is just what is needed, again.
explanation.definitionFit: To visit a place or person once more is to go and see them a second time.

clue.text: Hideous thing witnessed, I'm exasperated and traumatised initially

parts.note: a sigh is an exasperated exhalation

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of traumatised

explanation.surface: Someone sees something awful and admits to feeling frazzled and shaken.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seen is a spectacle, and a person looking a sight looks unattractive.

clue.text: Flier put away

definitions.meaning: a migratory bird with a forked tail
to eat or drink up, consume

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a forked-tailed bird and the act of gulping food down.

clue.text: Fire, when wire in copper frayed at the edges

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
frayed at the edges means the coin loses its outer letters

parts.note: a copper is a penny, a copper coin
the live is the charged conductor in a plug

explanation.surface: A fire breaks out when a wire inside a worn copper cable sparks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frayed at the edges' cuts PENNY to ENN; LIVE goes 'in' it. 'Fire' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone up is to rouse or animate them.

clue.text: When so decrepit, the steed finally put down

indicators.note: finally applies to each of the five words, picking its last letter

explanation.surface: An old horse so feeble it must be put to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put down' suggests destroying the horse; it means written down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something recorded in writing has been jotted or written down.

clue.text: Formal residence for the swine accommodating chief

indicators.note: accommodating means housing, so the sty holds the other piece

parts.note: pigs live in a sty
arch means chief, as in archenemy

explanation.surface: A pig's home with room for a pompous boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff, prim behaviour is called starchy, like a starched collar.

clue.text: Restriction applying to poultry

parts.note: a cap is a limit, as on spending
on means concerning or applying to

explanation.surface: A limit imposed on chicken farming.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrated cockerel fattened for the table is a kind of fowl.

clue.text: Leaves in spring gather against ledge, usually every second

indicators.note: every second here means the second letter of every word that follows

explanation.surface: In spring, foliage tends to pile up against a ledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like foliage but means sheets of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaf of a book is a sheet, each side a page.

clue.text: I'm off to work, boxes piled high

indicators.note: boxes means encloses, so the work surrounds the jumble

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: high means intoxicated, so the letters of piled are scrambled

explanation.surface: A worker leaving for the office with boxes stacked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' rearranges PILED into DELIP, which OP 'boxes'. This is a dated British farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: This jaunty old British goodbye is said by someone leaving.

clue.text: Step twit has climbed

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means read upwards

parts.note: a sap is a fool or twit

explanation.surface: A fool has climbed a step.
explanation.walkthrough: PAS is a dance step in ballet.
explanation.definitionFit: In ballet a pas is a single dance step.

clue.text: Lack of practice, with son no longer in the groove

indicators.note: no longer in means the son is removed from the word

parts.note: rust is deterioration from lack of practice

explanation.surface: An out-of-practice son no longer has his rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: A furrow or track worn into a surface, as by wheels.

clue.text: Game lit up, moments later

indicators.note: later places the moments after the drunk word

parts.note: lit up is slang for drunk, as is tiddly
winks are instants, as in in a wink

explanation.surface: A game: the drinker is merry, then sleeps a while later.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's pastime of flicking counters into a cup.
